subject: A taskq record quoted in a document must not become a task
description:
The result-side decode runs on EVERY tool result, not just a shell one, because a
tool_result carries only a tool_use_id and no tool name. So a session that READS a file
containing an example record picks it up as a real mutation.

Measured 2026-08-31: taskq-DESIGN.md section 9 prints a sample record verbatim
(op=claim, task=12, subject="Activity pane: humanize ETA"). Two unrelated sessions that had
read that doc both show a phantom task #12 in the panel. Reading this repos own
claude-replay-engine/src/engine/taskq.rs test fixtures does the same, and produced a
further eight subject-less stubs in the session that wrote them.

The v21 change that lets a create record stand its task up on its own makes these MORE
visible, which is the right trade for real tasks but sharpens this one.

Fix: gate the result-side decode on provenance -- only decode records from the result of a
shell call whose command actually invoked the taskq program. The call side already applies
that test (taskq_calls requires the word before the verb to be the program); the result
side cannot today because it has no access to the call.

That needs the adapter to carry a little state: remember the tool_use_ids of shell calls
whose command mentioned taskq, and decode a result only for those. Claude decode_line
already threads a &mut String cwd, so it has somewhere to put it; Codex has a
LinePreprocessor with real state. Both would need the set.

Cheaper partial: a record inside a Read result is far more suspicious than one in a Bash
result, but the tool name is not available at the result either, so this is the same
problem wearing a smaller hat.

Definition of done: reading taskq-DESIGN.md in a session creates no tasks; a session that
actually runs taskq is unchanged; a fixture covering both.
activeForm: Gating taskq records on call provenance
outcome:
Investigated first: real, narrow, and cheaper than the task assumed. Measured across every local transcript carrying the sentinel (15 of them): 786 occurrences at column 0, 19 indented, and of 377 distinct record ids exactly ONE appears only indented -- m2k9x1-ab3f, the sample record printed in taskq-DESIGN.md section 9. Two unrelated sessions that had merely READ that document showed its example ("Activity pane: humanize ETA") as a real task. Every indented occurrence of a genuine id also appears at column 0, so nothing real depends on the leniency.

So the fix is one line, not the stateful call/result provenance this task proposed: require the sentinel to BEGIN its line. taskq prints its records, so a real one starts at column 0; anything indented is a quotation -- a doc code block, a diff context line, a pretty-printed log. The earlier trim_start() was leniency with no evidence behind it.

Verified after: phantom sessions 2 -> 0 across all 15, and the agent-metrics session went 11 tasks/2 blank to 10 tasks/1 blank -- exactly the phantom removed and nothing else. Mutation-tested (restoring trim_start fails the new test). FOLD_VERSION 21 -> 22, byte gate PASS with no re-baseline. Ships in v1.121.0.

NOT closed by this: a record printed at column 0 by something other than taskq -- cat journal.ndjson, taskq history -- still decodes. That is by design (section 9 wants history echoes to reach the transcript, and rid dedupe makes repeats harmless), so the stateful provenance idea stays unbuilt and unneeded.

log.msg: Correction to this task description: the eight subject-less stubs (#108-#125) are NOT from taskq fixtures. Measured: this transcript carries 51 TaskCreate and 127 TaskUpdate calls from the harness NATIVE task tools, whose ids run in the 100s; those rows are ordinary #125 stubs from update-without-create and have nothing to do with taskq. The verified phantom is task #12 alone, from taskq-DESIGN.md section 9 example record (op=claim, subject "Activity pane: humanize ETA"), seen in two unrelated sessions that read that doc. One further symptom is UNEXPLAINED and belongs here: in the session that wrote this decoder, taskq task #9 still renders with #10 subject after the v21 fix. Two create records exist for id 9 in that transcript where the queue has one; suspected self-reference (the transcript contains the decoder own test fixtures and probe output as text), not reproduced in a clean session. Trace it before assuming the v21 pairing is at fault.
